symptom: signature mechanic shipped as a cosmetic effect (echoes-of-the-rift realm-shift was a screen tint + label, no terrain transform, absent in the dungeon scene)
rule: the signature mechanic MUST be expressed through the engine's content schema and pass the signature gate in the vertical slice before ANY content is expanded. If the schema can't express it, the design must be re-scoped — never fake it in render code.

symptom: generator/level-data/QA used different data shapes; reachability solver could not parse tiles -> infinite debug loop -> 188 backup files -> pipeline paused
rule: all content flows through ONE typed schema (content.schema.json + profile). The contract gate runs first and blocks; a shape mismatch fails in ms, never jams the loop.
evidence: pipeline_state.json l2_reachability 0/7 'Could not parse level data'

symptom: games scored 100/100 QA while being lifeless because QA only checked boot+reachability, never feel or genre fidelity
rule: a build is not done until the signature gate (mechanic exists), feel gate (plays to a resolution), and fidelity gate (looks like the genre) pass — functional-only QA is necessary but not sufficient.

symptom: xAI/PixelLab assets shipped with dark slate boxes around sprites (brightness-28 alpha key missed bg ~64), portrait frames used as walking sprites, blurry upscaled fonts
rule: every generated asset passes an art-coherence check before it reaches the game: alpha-key by corner-color distance not fixed brightness; sprite frames must be ~square for walking units; all in-game text uses FFG.text (resolution:2).

tactics maps must contain usable full-cover tiles adjacent to floor, reachable enemies, and units spawned on walkable tiles — the contract gate enforces spawn-on-walkable; the signature gate enforces cover-reduces-hit.

symptom: Kenney/Quaternius GLB models reference a sibling Textures/colormap.png by relative path
rule: when the asset step copies a GLB into a game, also copy its sibling Textures/ folder or models render untextured

symptom: claude -p slices omit top-level title and emit their own view shape (view:{camera,zoom,lookAt}); tactics slices sometimes place a unit on a wall/full-cover tile
rule: ALWAYS include top-level title + view:{width,height} (engine owns the camera; never put camera/zoom/lookAt in view). Tactics: every unit spawns on a floor tile (0), never on 1/3. The driver auto-normalizes title/view; the contract gate blocks bad unit placement.

symptom: Void Skirmish (tactics) shipped READY_TO_DEPLOY looking like programmer-art: units were coloured circles with a LETTER, cover was flat brown squares, hazards were a coffee-cup emoji. It passed because the fidelity (vision) gate was SOFT and, worse, never even ran — feel_and_fidelity() was called without a screenshot so fidelity was skipped, and READY_TO_DEPLOY was written regardless of gate results.
rule: feel + fidelity are BLOCKING for shipping. The fidelity gate captures its OWN in-game screenshot (via capture.py + a generic start-gameplay eval) and runs every build; a placeholder/non-genre/visually-unverified result HOLDS the build (HELD_NOT_SHIPPABLE marker, status 'held') instead of writing READY_TO_DEPLOY. The vision prompt auto-fails lettered-token units, emoji-as-sprites, and untextured debug grids. Genre renderers must ship real themed art (tactics now uses game-icons unit silhouettes + beveled cover + hazard tiles, not letters).
